review_scope: Model access was checked against host-observed reads, then those original physical pages were independently inspected. Additional reviewer pages are listed separately and were not read by the model.

papers.title: Response Quality Assessment for Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Conditional Conformal Factuality
Hybrid Retrieval for Retrieval Augmented Generation in the German Language Production Domain

supported_design_changes: Separate query-level calibration and final evaluation, and investigate automatic factuality-label errors.
Report the hybrid paper's question-hit measure separately from chunk precision and claim support.
Control chunk lengths, top-k and quota-merge configurations when comparing retrieval methods.
Retain explicit missing-method and search-freshness limitations.
corrections: No tool receipt supports additional Conformal-RAG pages 4 or 5; the observed pages 4 and 5 belong to the hybrid-retrieval paper.
The hybrid matching protocol permits one or two chunks, not two sentences.
Independent calibration and test queries do not require banning a shared fixed retrieval corpus; manage duplicate or related questions and tuning leakage separately.
The cosine-product claim score is specified in Algorithm 1, not the paper's Equation 1.
additional_reviewer_findings: Conformal page 3 conditions the guarantee on correct calibration annotations; the conditional experiment assumes pre-specified groups with labels available at inference.
Hybrid page 9 explicitly cautions about LLM-generated questions and direct lexical carry-over favoring full-text search. These limitations were added by the reviewer, not attributed to model reading.
remaining_work: Inspect code, supplements, detailed data separation and empirical result pages before implementation.
Validate annotation reliability and distribution assumptions in the intended deployment setting.
Refresh the matching search plan and consider other key work before a current-frontier or novelty claim.
